content: I’ll trace depfile loading, dyndep graph mutation, and scheduling order, then add a focused regression test before running the relevant test suite.

The likely failure is stale reverse graph state: a depfile node is loaded as a source before dyndep later assigns it a producing edge, so the already-scanned consumer is not reconsidered in the same build. I’m narrowing where dyndep refresh should invalidate or rescan that consumer without disturbing normal scheduling.
The root cause is now supported; I need only the complete dyndep refresh function to place the fix at the existing rescan boundary and preserve plan invariants.

I’ll implement the scanner fix by completing input traversal—including producers attached by dyndep—before deriving the consumer’s dirty/readiness state, and add an end-to-end regression that requires both the dyndep producer and depfile consumer to run in one build.

The patch transaction was rejected because the test insertion context was only partially visible, so no files changed. I’ll read exactly that local test block and reapply the same cohesive change with anchored context.

The implementation and regression are in place. I’m running the single new test first; if it passes, I’ll run the graph/build test groups and then inspect the final diff for scheduling and cycle edge cases.
